newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin meets Annan, says Russia will pay UN debts.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin meets Annan, says Russia will pay UN debts.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Saturday Russia would settle its debts to the United Nations and increase its cooperation with the organisation.

During a meeting in the Kremlin with Kofi Annan, Yeltsin praised the new Secretary-General's "energetic work" on reorganisation. Annan was to fly to St Petersburg later on Saturday and conclude a four-day visit to Russia on Sunday.
"We will develop our cooperation with the U.N.," Yeltsin said at the start of their meeting. "We will settle up, in a disciplined way as is planned, without creating new debts."
Russia is the second biggest debtor to the U.N., though its debts are a fraction of those of the United States, which owes well over half the organisation's $2.3 billion deficit.

Russia paid $305 million to the organisation last year and has promised to pay off the rest of its debts. In September last year it owed some $300 million for peacekeeping operations, which are the main component of member countries' debts to the U.N.

Annan told a news conference he had discussed a wide range of subjects with Yeltsin, including the treaty agreed between Russia and NATO last week which aims to calm Russian worries about the alliance's plan to invite east European countries to join. Annan said the treaty should increase global security.
Among other topics, he said he discussed ways of "enhancing" the U.N.'s activities in peacekeeping in the former Soviet Union in cooperation with Russia.
